report: Andrea was restless throughout the night, frequently getting out of bed and wandering the hallways. She seemed agitated and disoriented, and attempts to calm her were only briefly successful. Her walker was used to prevent falls, but she required assistance to be guided back to her room multiple times. A review of her nighttime medication is suggested to help her sleep more comfortably. Sleeps 1 hour straight hours before waking up.

Betty declined breakfast this morning, reporting severe nausea and a pain in her lower abdomen. Despite receiving anti-nausea medication, she vomited shortly after sipping on water. She has been placed on IV fluids to prevent dehydration, and a pain relief patch has been applied to her shoulder for management. Her skin appears pale and clammy, with minimal activity noted throughout the day.

Charles experienced severe shortness of breath in the afternoon, requiring supplemental oxygen and multiple rest periods. Despite his limited mobility, he insisted on visiting the common area. He used his wheelchair and was accompanied by a nurse on the walk. He participated minimally in social interactions and seemed very fatigued, needing assistance to return to his room afterwards. Immediate review by the respiratory team is recommended.

Dorothy showed increased levels of confusion and apathy throughout the morning; she did not recognize her family members during their visit. She skipped lunch and could only take a few sips of water. She lay in bed most of the day, needing full assistance with hygiene tasks but showing signs of agitation when repositioned. Her skin remains fragile, with the beginning stages of a pressure ulcer on her sacrum. Additional cushioning has been provided, and regular repositioning is scheduled.

Elena experienced sharp back pain during her evening shower, requiring immediate pain management. She was brought back to bed and assisted with her dental care and night routine fully. A hot pack was applied to her lower back, providing temporary relief. Doctor's visit required to review her pain medications for better control and possibly adjust her care plan to accommodate her limited mobility. Adjustable positioning in bed was advised to alleviate discomfort.

Andrea complained of significant back pain throughout the day and appeared very fatigued. She required full assistance for mobilisation and transferred to her wheelchair twice. Ate little during lunch, taking only a few spoons of soup. Anti-emetic administered, and subcutaneous fluids commenced due to dehydration concerns. Awaiting specialist review.

Jonathan showed signs of agitation and confusion during the morning hours, repeatedly asking to call his daughter. He needed encouragement to brush his teeth and dress. Missed breakfast, reporting feelings of nausea and dizziness. A minor adjustment in his pain medication was made after a consultation with the GP. Will monitor overnight.

Marie was quite restless overnight, frequently wandering in the room despite instructions to stay in bed. Increased shortness of breath noted; oxygen therapy was administered. She spent an extended time in the bathroom due to diarrhoea. Managed to eat a light meal with support but remains fatigued. Will conduct a care plan discussion tomorrow morning.

Daniel's nausea persisted throughout the day, intensely affecting his food intake. Vomiting episodes noted post meals. Subcutaneous hydration and prescribed anti-emetic medications administered. Skin checks showed slight redness around the lower back. Shifted to a pressure-relieving mattress and awaiting wound care team review.

Helen had an unsettling day marked by frequent complaints of pain and experiencing confusion. She seemed disoriented, requiring help with morning hygiene routines. Only managed to drink half a glass of water during lunch, citing queasiness. IM Zofran was administered, and subcutaneous fluids started in response to dehydration. Expected visit from family tomorrow may help boost morale.

Andrea remained restless throughout the night, frequently repositioning in bed and making several attempts to leave her room. She eventually fell asleep in the early hours but woke up disoriented. Her confusion was noted to be more intense this morning. Required full assistance with eating breakfast but managed only a few sips of tea. Reports of mild back pain and an itchy rash noted on her lower legs. GP consultation scheduled for tomorrow.

David experienced severe episodes of breathlessness overnight that required the use of oxygen therapy. He reported lower back pain and expressed discomfort due to a pressure ulcer on his sacrum. Despite encouragement, he ate very little of his breakfast. Interacted briefly with a fellow resident but appeared disinterested. Plans for adjusting his care plan with family are in the works.

Isabella was observed to be agitated and confused today, constantly repeating questions and pacing the hallways. She needed assistance with toileting multiple times due to incontinence and required partial help during her shower. Unable to consume lunch, displayed nausea, and vomited shortly after trying to eat. Carried out her afternoon resting in bed, awaiting a planned medical review.

John had several falls attempts during the evening and needed close supervision. Showed signs of severe apathy and was unresponsive to visitors. Refused breakfast outright and only took a small amount of water with much coaxing. His oedema in the legs appears to have worsened and his long nails were trimmed as they had become problematic. Consultations provided for a care plan revision.

Marie was restless and wandered during the night. She transitioned poorly from her wheelchair to bed this morning. Received full assistance with her morning routine but declined to brush her teeth. Inordinately confused and didn't recognize her surroundings but had occasional moments of lucidity. Complained of tightness in her chest and belching frequently. Medications have been adjusted by the attending nurse and family has been notified about her condition.

Andrea experienced severe nausea throughout the day. She could not manage to eat any solid food despite multiple efforts and required two doses of IM Zofran. Additionally, she was hydrated via subcutaneous fluids. A GP review is pending to reassess her current pain management and digestive care plan.

Richard showed signs of increased agitation and confusion in the evening. He repeatedly tried to leave his room and had to be redirected multiple times. Despite receiving his regular dose of antipsychotic medication, his restlessness did not fully subside. Scheduled a family meeting to discuss possible adjustments in his care regimen.

Carla developed severe back pain today, which limited her mobility significantly. She reported the pain being constant and worsening when sitting or standing. Nursing staff administered prescribed pain relief, yet there was minimal improvement. Concerning her condition, a specialist consultation has been requested.

Samuel required full assistance with eating this morning. He choked briefly on pureed food but managed to continue with encouragement. He remains on a hydration protocol, and caregivers have noted decreased fluid intake. Suggested reviewing his swallowing assessment to update nutritional guidelines.

Maria appeared apathy and confusion worsened significantly today. She was less responsive during interactions and displayed difficulty recognizing staff members. There is a notable decline in her cognitive status, prompting an urgent evaluation with her primary care physician and adjustment in her medication for improved alertness and orientation.

Andrea experienced severe nausea and was unable to consume her lunch. She was given anti-emetic medication and laid down for an hour. When she tried to eat toast later, she vomited immediately. Since then, she hasn't consumed any food or water. She's now on subcutaneous fluids and has received IM Zofran. We're waiting for the GP review.

Bella had difficulty washing and dressing herself this morning and required full assistance. She shows signs of restlessness and mild agitation, making it hard to perform these tasks efficiently. Her family has requested an update on her condition and wants to discuss her care plan further. We will be arranging a meeting with them soon.

Carl struggled with his appetite at breakfast and only managed to eat a few spoonfuls of oatmeal with encouragement. Despite the use of adapted cutlery and cups, he choked twice, raising concerns about his ability to swallow safely. We are maintaining a close watch on his hydration and nutrition. His family has been informed.

Deidre has shown increased restlessness and confusion, especially at nighttime. She frequently gets out of bed and wanders, necessitating constant monitoring. In addition, her nails are excessively long, and she has developed mild redness on her heels, potentially indicating early-stage pressure ulcers. Staying alert to her demands requires heightened attention from the night staff.

Edward received a visitor today, which appeared to improve his mood significantly. He spent the afternoon browsing through a magazine with assistance and briefly interacted with other residents during an organized activity. Nevertheless, he complained of back pain and had difficulty sitting comfortably in his wheelchair. Pain management and ergonomic adjustments are being considered.
